traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 335 Polemoniaceae: annual to perennial herbs, rarely shrubs; leaves alternate or opposite, entire or palmately or pinnately divided; flowers regular, rarely nearly two-lipped, often crowded in corymbs or heads; sepals 5, joined; corolla of 5 united petals, a tube; stamens 5 on the corolla; ovary superior, of 3 (rarely 2) cells; fruit a capsule, rarely staying shut. The phloxes' salver-shaped corolla is from common knowledge, inferred.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Polemoniaceae with Cobaeaceae: its irregular flowers have a two-lipped corolla, read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy bilabiate. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 393, 396, family Polemoniaceae: stipules false; read as false.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add rotate (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 393, 396: rotate, salverform or bilabiate.

traits.inflorescence.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add solitary (sometimes), cyme (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 393, 396: head, cyme or solitary.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add whorled (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 393, 396: alternate, opposite or whorled.
